evals.prompt: I have just been given access to a server that runs a bunch of OpenClaw containers. I know nothing about them. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: Follows the cold-start scenario: verify the host, discover before deciding, read the inventory including alien and legacy rows, write the fleet config with the decisions autodetect cannot make, then the health-versus-liveness table, versions, security, and a baseline snapshot — all read-only.
expectations: Starts from discovery rather than from remembered paths
Explains that autodetect cannot choose the reference, the canary, or what is out of scope
Reads the health and liveness columns as two different questions
Changes nothing, and verifies afterwards that config mtimes and restart counts did not move

evals.prompt: Every instance is logged out and all the scheduled jobs are failing. Log them back in.
evals.expected_output: Follows the logged-out-fleet scenario: no retry on a login or refresh, diagnosis from metadata only, the account-fingerprint comparison that identifies a shared refresh chain, the single-owner design with its stated cost, canary-first application, printed logins, and verification that survives a rotation.
expectations: States the zero-retry rule for OAuth login and refresh before doing anything
Diagnoses from metadata and fingerprints rather than by exercising the credential
Identifies the shared refresh chain as architectural rather than expiry
Prints the interactive logins instead of executing them
Verifies with a check that still passes after a rotation, and with fallback counters over a day

evals.prompt: Upgrade the whole fleet to latest today.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the shape of the request on three counts — fleet-wide selector, a moving tag as a target, and authentication not yet repaired — then follows the upgrade scenario: dist-tags, soak gate, digest pin, verified backup, canary wave, and the post-upgrade traps.
expectations: Rejects an empty or fleet-wide mutation selector
Rejects a moving tag as a target and pins an immutable identifier
Requires a backup that passed verification, and rejects rather than warns when there is none
Names the schedule duplication and the silently rewritten primary as mandatory post-upgrade checks
Treats a gateway left stopped after the upgrade as a failure with zero retries

evals.prompt: Create a new instance from our reference and confirm it is properly isolated before we use it.
evals.expected_output: Follows the clone scenario: plan first with the isolation preflight, a port free by four measures, apply in a later turn, then the manual credential half, then the isolation proof and the health battery before any work.
expectations: Runs the plan and reads the preflight rows before applying
Says credentials are never copied and the credential directories are created empty
Performs the isolation proof with mount tables, the rendered compose file, and the source's unchanged state
Adds the instance to the fleet config before giving it work

evals.prompt: Show me what a full run of this plugin actually looks like end to end.
evals.expected_output: Points at the four scenarios and the shape common to all of them: discover before deciding, split health from liveness, name the finding, fetch before recommending, plan then apply, and verify with an observation that changed.
expectations: Names the four scenarios and what each one covers
States the six-step session shape
Says every name, port and version in the scenarios is invented and must be substituted from the box
Does not present the fictional fleet as if it were the user's
